content: Avemar, a wheat germ extract, is prescribed with specific dosing based on the indication. For individuals weighing less than 90 kg, the recommended dose is 9 grams orally once daily. For those weighing more than 90 kg, the dose is 9 grams orally twice daily. The powder should be mixed in 150 mL of water or another liquid that does not contain vitamin C. It should be taken one hour before meals. Clinical trials have demonstrated significant benefits of Avemar in certain cancers, particularly colorectal cancer. Small clinical studies have shown improvements in progression-free survival and overall survival, as well as the absence of metastases in colorectal cancer patients compared to control groups. These findings were published in the British Journal of Cancer (2003) and Hepato-Gastroenterology (2000). Additional studies suggest survival benefits in melanoma and quality-of-life improvements in breast cancer patients. Avemar is approved in Hungary as a medical nutrient. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) has been shown to decrease the effects of wheat germ extract through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and it is recommended to separate the administration of Avemar and vitamin C by at least two hours. Similarly, rose hips also reduce the effects of wheat germ extract via an unknown mechanism, and the same two-hour separation is advised. Wheat germ extract may enhance the effects of tamoxifen through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination is considered beneficial in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, but close monitoring is required. Adverse effects associated with Avemar include soft stools, nausea, and diarrhea. It is contraindicated in patients with malabsorption syndrome, gastrointestinal ulcers, celiac disease, gluten sensitivity, those undergoing transplants, individuals with inherited fructose intolerance, and those with hypersensitivity to the product. Avemar should only be administered when the patient has been able to tolerate oral food intake without complications for at least four days. Other medicinal products or supplements, particularly those containing vitamin C, should be given at least two hours apart. Avemar is not recommended during pregnancy or lactation. It falls under Pregnancy Category: Avoid, as there is insufficient evidence to confirm safety during these periods.
